question: Which of the following is included in the foundational 'Six Rights' of medication administration?

options.A: Right nurse, right room, right time
options.B: Right patient, right medication, right dose
options.C: Right diagnosis, right doctor, right family
options.D: Right hospital, right equipment, right cost

explanation: The Six Rights include right patient, right medication, right dose, right route, right time, and right documentation, which are essential for safe administration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h1)

question: What is the primary reason for a nurse to observe universal precautions and hand hygiene before an injection?

options.A: To save time during a busy shift
options.C: To comply with hospital fashion codes
options.D: To ensure the medication dissolves properly

explanation: Aseptic technique and hand hygiene are critical infection control measures used to prevent healthcare-associated infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which intramuscular injection site is widely considered the safest and preferred site for adult patients?
explanation: The ventrogluteal site is preferred for adults because it lacks major nerves and blood vessels and provides a thick muscle mass. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: When administering a subcutaneous injection in the abdominal area, which zone must be avoided?
explanation: Nurses must avoid a 2-inch radius around the umbilicus when giving subcutaneous abdominal injections to prevent tissue trauma. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the standard angle of insertion for an intradermal injection?
explanation: Intradermal injections are given at a shallow angle of 5 to 15 degrees to place the medication just beneath the epidermis. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which parenteral route provides immediate systemic bioavailability by delivering the drug directly into the bloodstream?
explanation: Intravenous injections or infusions deliver medications directly into a vein, achieving immediate systemic availability. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: What does a higher needle gauge number indicate regarding the needle's diameter?
explanation: Needle gauge is inversely related to diameter; a higher gauge number means a smaller needle lumen diameter. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: Why are safety-engineered devices, such as sliding shields or retractable needles, utilized during injections?

options.A: To make the injection process faster
options.B: To decrease the cost of medical supplies

explanation: Safety-engineered devices are specifically designed to protect healthcare workers by preventing accidental needlestick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: What special device must be used when withdrawing medication from a snapped glass ampoule to protect the patient?

options.D: A blunt-fill cannula without a filter

explanation: A filter needle must be used when drawing medication from a glass ampoule to trap any microscopic glass shards that may have fallen inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of injecting air into a closed vial before withdrawing medication?

options.C: To equalize pressure and ease withdrawal
options.D: To activate the chemical properties of the drug

explanation: Injecting air into a vial creates positive pressure, which counteracts a vacuum and makes withdrawing the fluid much easier. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why must an antiseptic skin swab be allowed to air dry completely before inserting the needle?

options.A: To prevent the alcohol from burning the patient and to ensure antimicrobial action
options.B: To cool the skin surface down
options.C: To make the skin stickier for the needle
options.D: To evaporate any excess air bubbles

explanation: Allowing the antiseptic to dry ensures it achieves maximum microbial kill and prevents stinging when the needle penetrates the skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: What is the correct action to take with a used needle immediately after administering an injection?

options.A: Recap the needle carefully using two hands
options.B: Place it on the bedside table for later disposal
options.C: Engage the safety device and discard directly into a sharps container
options.D: Break the needle off before disposal

explanation: Used needles should have their safety devices engaged and be immediately discarded into a puncture-resistant sharps container without manual recapping. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of using the Z-track method for intramuscular injections?

options.A: To make the needle enter the skin faster
options.B: To prevent irritating or staining medications from leaking into subcutaneous tissue
options.C: To eliminate the need for skin antisepsis
options.D: To speed up the systemic absorption rate indefinitely

explanation: The Z-track method seals the needle track as the skin snaps back, preventing irritating drugs from leaking into subcutaneous tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h7)

question: How long should the nurse wait after injecting medication before withdrawing the needle when using the Z-track method?
explanation: Keeping the needle inserted for approximately 10 seconds allows the medication to disperse fully into the muscle tissue before the track is unsealed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h7)

question: Which of the following practices is strictly prohibited to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries?

options.B: Placing sharps containers at the point of care
options.D: Disposing of uncapped needles in a rigid container

explanation: Two-handed recapping is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries and is strictly prohibited in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: Improper placement of an intramuscular injection in which anatomical site is most likely to cause injury to the sciatic nerve?
explanation: The dorsogluteal site runs close to the sciatic nerve, making improper injections in this area a high risk for nerve damage. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: When is the most appropriate time for a nurse to document an administered injection?

options.C: At the end of the shift

explanation: Documentation must occur immediately after the medication is administered to ensure accuracy and prevent potential dosing errors. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h9)

question: Which of the following details must be included when documenting an injection in the patient's record?

options.A: The cost of the medication and brand name
options.B: The anatomical site used and route
options.C: The weather conditions at the time

explanation: Accurate injection documentation requires recording the medication name, dose, route, exact anatomical site, date, time, and nurse's signature. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h9)
